name: Warehouse
lineup: Shipments import before the truck arrives, receiving is a scan, and every piece already knows which job it belongs to.

seo.title: Warehouse — Kickback
seo.description: Warehouse turns supplier load sheets into shipments, receives and racks material by scan, and shows which jobs have everything in.
seo.ogDescription: Load sheets import themselves. Pieces scan in, scan onto racks, and each job shows when its material is all here.

hero.headlineHtml: Know where every piece is, from truck to install.
hero.lede: Your supplier's load sheet becomes a shipment before the truck pulls in. The dock scans pieces off the truck and onto racks, and each job shows the moment all of its material is here.
hero.metaHtml: Part of the Kickback Platform · Billed per paired scanner

sections.title: Works With
sections.note: Load sheets and ship notices from these suppliers import as shipments.

sections.title: From Load Sheet to Install
sections.lede: Connect your CRM and your suppliers once. After that, the warehouse runs on scans.

items.title: The Manifest Imports Itself
items.body: Your supplier emails the load sheet to the address Kickback gives you, or you upload it. Every PO, bundle and serial lands as a shipment, and each order links to its CRM job by PO number.

items.title: Scan It In, Scan It Away
items.body: The dock scans each piece, or a bundle label once, as it comes off the truck. Scan a rack label and the piece, or its whole order, is put away there.

items.title: Pull What's Ready
items.body: A job is ready once every shipping line is received. When it's scheduled, the picker gets a route through the racks and stages each piece by scan.

items.title: Shipments Import Themselves
items.body: Each supplier connection gets its own manifest email address. Your supplier sends load sheets there, or you drop the file on the Manifests page. Kickback reads the PO, bundle and serial on every line and builds the shipment before the truck shows up.

bullets.title: Matched to the Right Job
bullets.text: Orders link to CRM jobs on an exact PO match. Anything less certain stays Unmatched with the three closest jobs, so material never lands on the wrong customer.

bullets.title: Every Line Accounted For
bullets.text: The import report marks each line Created, Updated, Order only or Rejected. A bad line is set aside and the rest of the load still lands.

bullets.title: Revised Load Sheets
bullets.text: Send a new sheet for the same BOL and the shipment updates in place. Pieces already received stay received.

bullets.title: New Shipment Alerts
bullets.text: When a manifest creates a shipment, your warehouse team gets a push.

items.title: Receive and Put Away by Scan
items.body: Scan each piece as it comes off the truck, or scan a bundle strap once to receive everything in it. Then scan a rack label to put a piece away, or its whole order at once. Scan or type any serial, PO or BOL into search and the record opens.

bullets.title: Locations and Floor Plans
bullets.text: Print a QR or barcode label for every rack. Draw the building with walls, dock doors and aisles, then tap a rack to see what's on it.

bullets.title: Pair a Scanner With One Code
bullets.text: A manager names the gun, like Dock 1, and gets a one-time pairing code. The gun scans it and from then on it's locked to Warehouse.

bullets.title: Revoke at Once
bullets.text: Lose a gun and press Revoke. It stops working on its next request.

bullets.title: Billed by Scanner
bullets.text: You pay for each paired scanner. Floor staff accounts don't add to the bill, so add everyone who works the warehouse.

items.title: Know What's Ready to Install
items.body: Each job lists its contract lines and the pieces received against each one. Once every shipping line is in, the job moves to Ready to Schedule on the Jobs list.

bullets.title: Scheduling Follows Your CRM
bullets.text: When the office books the install in your CRM, every received piece on that job is scheduled. Unbook it and they go back to received.

bullets.title: Pick Routes and Pick Sheets
bullets.text: The Pick page walks the floor plan rack by rack and ends at a dock door. Print it as a pick sheet, with or without the map.

bullets.title: Staged by Scan
bullets.text: The picker scans each piece to stage it. When the last one is staged, your warehouse team gets a push.

bullets.title: Needs Attention
bullets.text: A job your CRM canceled or unbooked while pieces were already moving gets flagged, with what to put back.

items.title: Consumables
items.body: Caulk, coil, shims and screws are counted by scan, and each one has a reorder point. Kickback works out what your open jobs will use from their contract lines, so the projected count already takes out what's owed.

bullets.title: Usage Rates
bullets.text: Set what each product category uses, like feet of coil per window. Override it for a single product when it differs.

bullets.title: Pulled Against the Job
bullets.text: Pulls on the pick screen are recorded against the job, so each job shows what it still owes.

bullets.title: New Barcodes Don't Stop the Dock
bullets.text: Scan something nobody has entered yet and it's counted under Needs a Name. Name it later.

bullets.title: Reorder and Short on the Dashboard
bullets.text: The dashboard counts what's at its reorder point and what open jobs will run short on.

sections.title: Automatic vs. You Confirm
sections.lede: Kickback keeps the counts. Anything that could put material on the wrong job waits for a person.

automatic.title: Automatic
items: Emailed load sheets import as shipments
Orders link to jobs on an exact PO match

sections.title: Works With Your Other Apps
sections.lede: Warehouse runs on the same CRM jobs and supplier connections as the rest of Kickback.

items.body: Connect Associated Materials or Wincore once. Costing gets the invoices, Warehouse gets the load sheets, and both land on the same CRM jobs.
Follow-Up works your open estimates. Once a job sells and its order ships, Warehouse tracks the material to install.

items.q: Which suppliers does Warehouse import from?
items.a: MI Windows and Doors, Associated Materials and Wincore. Wincore ship notices list orders without serial numbers, so Wincore pieces can't be scanned in yet.

items.q: How does Warehouse decide a job is ready?
items.a: You choose which product categories arrive from a supplier. A job is ready when every line in those categories has its full quantity received. Broken and mismeasured pieces don't count.

items.q: Do we need scanners to use it?
items.a: No. Receiving, put-away and search work in any browser, and you can type into every scan box. Paired scanners give the floor a shared login that only opens Warehouse.
By paired scanner. The plan includes one, and you can add more. Floor staff accounts don't count, and revoking a scanner frees its slot.

items.q: What if a scanner goes missing?
items.a: Revoke it in Warehouse settings. It stops working on its next request and needs a new pairing code to come back.
Book a demo. Kickback sets up your account, then you connect your CRM and suppliers, print rack labels and pair a scanner. The setup guide in Warehouse walks through each step.
